description: Issue #839 AC2, the cross-kind collision in the STRUCT-FIRST direction: `struct tally [ x y ]` then `define tally`. Its mirror (`define` then `struct`) is `struct-reserved-word-procedure`. Having both directions is what makes the pair meaningful: an implementation that only checked a `struct` name against already-declared procedures — but not a `define` name against already-declared structs — would report the mirror and be silent here, so this fixture is the one that fails for it. `spec/error-model.md:126` covers exactly this case: "a procedure and a struct with the same name in either order". Note what neither direction can show: whether the runtime keeps one first-declaration map or two with a cross-kind lookup — those are indistinguishable from source, so no description here claims it. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`.
